issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: the type checker rejects `self.f` (symbol_resolver.go 'undefined member'), so no BIR is produced -> frontend. It is a diagnostic, not a Go panic, so no frontend-crash. A clean-context spec check found the program VALID: §6.10 says a field access naming an object method gives a new function value bound to the object, and the expected output is `1`. Related but not a duplicate: #1215 (open, frontend). There `a.get` from outside the class compiles but crashes at runtime with an interface-conversion error; I verified it still does on main. Both need method-value support for field access, so a fix should cover both. Consider linking them.

issues.title: [Bug]: a variable read in an expression sees changes made by a later sub-expression
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The BIR is wrong: for `[v, bump()]`, --dump-bir shows `%1 = bump()` and then `newArray [...]{v, %1}`, so the module variable `v` is read after the call. BIR generation does not snapshot the variable into a temporary, so this is frontend (invalid BIR), not runtime. A clean-context spec check found the list constructor (§6.7.1), the function arguments (§6.15) and the closure-captured local all definitely violate the spec; each must print [1,2]. For the mapping constructor and binary `+`, the spec text does not strictly state an evaluation order, though left-to-right is the clear intent. One root cause covers every case. No duplicate found. Related but distinct evaluation-order issues: #1217 (compound member assignment), #511 (check desugaring reorders operands) and #1166 (named args evaluated in parameter order).

issues.title: [Bug]: named argument rejected for the implicit rest field of an inclusive included-record parameter
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: no included record parameter accepts named argument 'count'
  --> i1573.bal:13:30
   |
13 |     io:println(describe("a", count = 3)); // @output a {"count":3}
   |                              ^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: SEMANTIC_ERROR 'no included record parameter accepts named argument' on a valid program, so frontend. It is a diagnostic, not a crash. A clean-context spec check found the program VALID: §5.4.2.2 says `record { F }` is equivalent to `record {| F; anydata...; |}`, and the §6.15 conditions all hold (a never-optional field for each parameter name, no other fields, only one included-record-param). Expected output is `a {"count":3}` then `b {}`. Not a duplicate. Related: #488 (closed, explicit-rest case, now works) and #1452 (open, a different path where an inclusive record included in an exclusive record loses its implicit rest). Both likely share a helper that ignores the implicit rest of inclusive records.
